subject: Post-demo: log export/playbook and sample extracts for MedSys security review
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Patel <j.patel@medsys.health>
Cc: Markus Reilly <markus.reilly@medsys.health>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo: log export/playbook and sample extracts for MedSys security review

Hi Jasmine / Markus —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and action items coming out of the security/data handling portion so your team has what you need to sign off on the next phase of the pilot.

1) What you asked for (summary)
- Example export that shows "who / when / action / resource id" for user-driven requests and API calls (including session id and source IP).
- Clarification on whether PII is present in logs or redacted/hashed by default and options for on-the-fly redaction.
- Retention policy and how to configure retention windows per environment (prod vs staging).
- Preferred export formats for your ingestion pipeline (you mentioned Parquet + S3).
- A short playbook describing how to request an ad-hoc export for a specific time range and how we deliver evidence packs for audits.

2) What we can provide immediately
- Attached: redwood-log-schema-v2.csv (column-level schema for the access logs we surface) — includes field definitions, examples, and notes on which fields may contain user-supplied content.
- Attached: s3-export-manifest-example.json (shows manifest layout we write to the customer's S3 export bucket).
- We typically store logs as gzipped JSONL in S3 (default), but we can run a one-off Parquet conversion for audit packages.

3) Questions we need from you to finalize the sample
- For Parquet: confirm if you require nested types (structs) or a flattened table (we can produce either).
- Time range: please confirm the window you want for the sample extract (default request is 7 days).
- Redaction: do you want raw logs (with PII masked via hashing) or redacted logs (PII removed) for the sample?
- Any format preferences for IP addresses (v4/v6 string, or anonymized)?

4) Proposed timeline
- We can generate a sample extract (JSONL + Parquet one-off) within 3 business days once you confirm the time range and redaction preference.
- Playbook draft (how to request exports, retention adjustment steps, and proof-of-access steps) — 2 business days.

Next steps: Jasmine, can you confirm time window (e.g., 2027-01-04 to 2027-01-10) and whether you want hashed or redacted PII in the sample? I’ll loop in Sergio to produce the export and Laura to include the playbook and delivery checklist.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-log-schema-v2.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
Attachment: s3-export-manifest-example.json (JSON, 3 KB)
From: Jasmine Patel <j.patel@medsys.health>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Reilly <markus.reilly@medsys.health>, MedSys Security Team <security@medsys.health>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log export/playbook and sample extracts for MedSys security review

Thanks Tessa — this is perfect and clear. A few quick answers so you can proceed: 

- Time window: yes, please use 2027-01-04T00:00:00Z through 2027-01-10T23:59:59Z for the sample.
- PII preference: For the first pass, please provide hashed PII (deterministic hash) plus a redacted variant in a separate file. Security wants to see the hashed view to validate mapping and the redacted view to validate removal.
- Parquet flavor: flattened table is preferred to make ingestion simpler for our data team. Nested structs are OK if it simplifies conversion, but flattened is primary preference.
- IPs: keep as strings (v4/v6) but include a boolean column ip_anonymized = true/false if an anonymization step was applied.

Also — for audit purposes, can you include a small sample (10 rows) that shows SSO user mapping to corporate identity (e.g., redwood_user_id -> medsys_user_id) so our identity team can verify the linkage? We do not need full user lists, just a proof of mapping for the sample timeframe.

If you can confirm that output is delivered to our staging bucket (s3://medsys-staging-exports/rdw-samples/), that will speed up ingestion on our end.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Patel
Lead Security Engineer, MedSys Health
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Patel <j.patel@medsys.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log export/playbook and sample extracts for MedSys security review

On Mon, Jan 11, 2027 at 10:02 AM Jasmine Patel <j.patel@medsys.health> wrote:
> If you can confirm that output is delivered to our staging bucket (s3://medsys-staging-exports/rdw-samples/), that will speed up ingestion on our end.

Hi all — quick operational note from infra: our standard pipeline writes gzipped JSONL to customer S3 by default. We can absolutely do the following for MedSys as a one-time sample: 

- Produce the 2027-01-04 -> 2027-01-10 extract as both: (A) gzipped JSONL (raw), (B) flattened Parquet (one-off conversion).
- Provide two variants for PII: deterministic-hashed columns AND a separate redacted file where sensitive columns are blanked.
- Include mapping sample (10 rows) for redwood_user_id -> medsys_user_id; we will mask medsys internal email addresses except for org-local ids per your request.
- Add ip_anonymized boolean column and include source_ip column as string for the sample.

Delivery: we can stage the export to s3://medsys-staging-exports/rdw-samples/ in a folder named sample-20270104-20270110/ within 3 business days. The export will include a manifest (see attached manifest example) and md5 checksums for delivered files.

Attached I’m adding a short procedure doc that describes how we run a one-off Parquet conversion and the QA steps we run before uploading. If you need this as an automated recurring export, we can scope that as part of the pilot (additional configuration and cost).

Let me know if you want the parquet schema to include union types or if strict simple types only — default will be simple primitive types for compatibility.

Sergio
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: one-off-parquet-procedure.docx (DOCX, 22 KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Patel <j.patel@medsys.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Reilly <markus.reilly@medsys.health>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log export/playbook and sample extracts for MedSys security review

Perfect — thanks Jasmine and Sergio. Next steps and owner assignments: 

- Sergio: produce both filesets (gzipped JSONL + flattened Parquet) for 2027-01-04 -> 2027-01-10, include hashed and redacted variants + the 10-row user mapping sample. Upload to s3://medsys-staging-exports/rdw-samples/sample-20270104-20270110/ and post the manifest. Due: EOD Thu 2027-01-14.
- Laura: I’ll send the export playbook + evidence checklist to Markus and Jasmine once Sergio confirms the manifest layout (ETA Tomorrow).
- Jasmine / MedSys: once uploaded, please confirm you can access the staging bucket and that your ingestion pipeline accepts the flattened Parquet. If anything fails we’ll iterate on the schema.

If we hit all items this week, we can move to contract redlines for a pilot scoped with weekly retention at 90 days and a SOC2 evidence handoff process.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with a short Loom to walk through the manifest/details after Sergio uploads.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
